items.name: S&P 500 (VFV + SPY)
items.street: Strategists are split: earnings are still growing, but the market is leaning on a handful of AI names while yields and oil stay high.
items.take: Crowd mood on the S&P 500 is about as gloomy as it gets, while the index itself has barely pulled back. Your VFV and SPY move together, so this is the sentiment that matters most for you.

TPU chips are seen as a $100B+ opportunity and a challenge to Nvidia

items.name: Alphabet
items.street: Strong Buy from 62 analysts; average target about $421–431, roughly a third above Friday's $317 close. Q3 consensus: revenue about $127.5B (+25%), EPS about $3.
items.take: The crowd is divided into two camps: a Cloud blowout sends it higher, a capex hike sends it lower. Your call is about $13 below its $330 strike, so the Oct 28 reaction matters a lot for its value.

items.take: Retail traders are more upbeat on Amazon than on Alphabet going into earnings. Your call is about $12 below its $260 strike; AWS growth vs. the 30–35% range is the swing factor.

mood.summary: Investors are nervous. The Fear & Greed index has sat in Extreme Fear for two weeks, and bearish individual investors outnumber bulls by about 9 points, well below the long-run norm. The S&P 500 fell for a second week and is about 2.5% off its Oct 6 record, while the Nasdaq is about 6% off after its worst day since June on Oct 22. Worries centre on AI spending, oil above $110 on Middle East tensions, and a possible Fed hike in December. Very fearful readings have often come before rebounds, but they don't say when.

items.name: SK Hynix ADR
items.about: American depositary receipt for SK Hynix, the Korean maker of DRAM and high-bandwidth memory chips used in AI servers.
items.why: The ADR closed up 1.9% at $145.36, then jumped about 8.4% to $154.62 in overnight trading. Posts say SK Hynix reported record third-quarter results (revenue near $78.9B, operating margin around 80%) and that its DRAM and HBM supply is effectively sold out through 2029; I could not confirm those figures independently. Posts also say Korea's KOSPI rose about 6%, lifting other memory names.

items.name: Robinhood Markets
items.about: Operates the Robinhood app for commission-free stock, options and crypto trading, plus retirement and card products.
items.why: Shares closed up 1.9% at $94.56, then fell about 5.8% to $87.48 after hours. Posts attribute the drop to the company's quarterly report, which came after the close, but I could not find coverage confirming the numbers, so the cause is unconfirmed.

items.name: Boeing
items.about: Aircraft maker with commercial jets, defense and space businesses.
items.why: Boeing closed down 10.7% at $168.18, near its low of the day, after its quarterly report. Market wraps that day tied the slide to a lower delivery target and a later 737 production timeline. Posts also cite an upgrade to Buy with a $250 target on Monday.

items.name: Seagate Technology
items.about: Makes hard disk drives and data storage systems, with growing demand from AI data centers.
items.why: Shares rose 3.7% to $667.85 into the report, then fell about 5.5% after hours to $631.23 even though results beat. Per posts, adjusted EPS was $7.68 versus $7.39 expected, revenue rose 61% to $4.2B, and next-quarter guidance topped estimates; posts say traders took profits after a recent rally and an analyst flagged slowing margin growth.

items.name: Enphase Energy
items.about: Makes solar microinverters, home batteries and energy management systems.
items.why: Shares closed down 2.0% at $29.76, then fell about 17% to $25.20 after hours following the third-quarter report. The company's release shows revenue of $293.3M, at the low end of its guidance range, with sell-through up only about 1% against 10% expected and European sell-through down 12%; posts say next-quarter guidance points to roughly a 30% year-over-year decline.

items.name: Candel Therapeutics
items.about: Clinical-stage biotech developing viral immunotherapies for cancer, led by CAN-2409 for prostate cancer.
items.why: Shares rose 5.9% to $8.25. Posts link the interest to the ESMO oncology conference, where Johnson & Johnson showed first data for its RIPTAC prostate-cancer drug that a J&J executive called the best the company had seen, and to Candel's own Phase 3 CAN-2409 result in localized prostate cancer. Traders are weighing whether the J&J news helps or competes with Candel.

items.name: Innodata
items.about: Provides data engineering and annotation services used to train and run AI models.
items.why: Shares closed down 25.3% at $44.74, with most of the loss coming in a sharp morning drop. Posts say the company announced layoffs and note earnings are coming; I could not find news confirming the cause of the drop.

items.name: United States Oil Fund
items.about: Exchange-traded fund that tracks the price of WTI crude oil futures.
items.why: The fund closed down 1.4% at $163.88 as oil eased on hopes of Middle East de-escalation, with WTI near $100. Posts say Israeli election exit polls are deadlocked and cite a Houthi claim of a missile strike on a Saudi refinery, which nudged crude up in evening trading.

items.name: Roundhill Memory ETF
items.about: ETF holding memory-chip makers such as Micron, SK Hynix and Samsung.
items.why: The fund rose 4.5% to $50.52 and gained another 7.8% after hours. Posts tie the move to SK Hynix's reported record results and a roughly 6% jump in Korea's KOSPI, which lifted memory stocks in extended trading.

items.name: Alphabet (Class C)
items.about: Parent of Google, Search, YouTube, Google Cloud and Waymo; Class C shares have no voting rights.
items.why: Shares closed up 0.8% at $316.83 and rose 2.6% after hours on a Reuters-cited report from The Information that OpenAI plans to buy Google's AI chips (TPUs). Alphabet reports third-quarter results Wednesday after the close; analysts expect about $3.02 EPS on $128.2B revenue, with Cloud growth and capex in focus.

items.name: Critical Metals
items.about: Mining company developing the Tanbreez heavy rare earths project in Greenland.
items.why: Shares jumped 27.4% to $8.13, with most of the gain in the afternoon. Posts link the buying to Greenland rare-earth enthusiasm and the pending all-stock acquisition of European Lithium (about $835M, which would give it full ownership of Tanbreez); posts also mention a large seller at $8.13 and a share sale. I could not confirm what triggered today's move.

items.name: Alphabet (Class A)
items.about: Parent of Google, Search, YouTube, Google Cloud and Waymo; Class A shares carry voting rights.
items.why: Shares closed up 1.2% at $320.58 and rose about 2.9% after hours after The Information reported that OpenAI plans to buy Google's TPU chips. The third-quarter report is due Wednesday after the close, and posts are split between expecting a big move up and worrying about capex and search.

items.name: Corning
items.about: Makes specialty glass, optical fiber and connectivity products used in phones, displays and AI data centers.
items.why: Shares closed down 1.1% at $126.30 after trading as high as $128.48, and have slipped over the past week. Posts tie the interest to optical-connectivity demand from AI data-center buildouts and mention a Citi Buy rating with a $200 target (lowered from $220), which I could not verify.

items.name: Figure Technology
items.about: Fintech that uses blockchain to originate and trade home-equity loans and other consumer credit.
items.why: Shares rose 4.2% to $22.84, then gave back some ground after hours at $22.52. Posts argue over short covering versus a longer decline and say the stock is down roughly 11% over the week; no company news was cited, so there is no clear catalyst.

items.name: Vertiv Holdings
items.about: Makes power and cooling equipment for data centers.
items.why: Shares rose 4.4% to $208.56 ahead of third-quarter results expected Wednesday morning, per posts. Vertiv also closed its roughly $1.45B acquisition of UtilityInnovation Group, a data-center power specialist, with up to $1.15B more in earnouts.

items.name: Micron Technology
items.about: Major maker of DRAM and NAND memory chips.
items.why: Shares rose 2.8% to $928.76 and added about 6.1% after hours to $958.75. Posts connect the move to SK Hynix's reported record quarter and the Korean market rally, and say memory stocks had been punished for months despite strong earnings.

items.name: Advanced Micro Devices
items.about: Designs CPUs, GPUs and AI accelerators for PCs, gaming and data centers.
items.why: Shares rose 5.5% to $560.26 and gained another 6.7% after hours. Posts credit the broad chip rally and AMD marketing around Meta's use of its EPYC processors, with traders watching Alphabet and Microsoft calls Wednesday for AMD mentions.

items.name: Adobe
items.about: Software maker behind Photoshop, Acrobat, Firefly and Experience Cloud.
items.why: Shares closed down 4.0% at $248.36 and slipped further after hours. Posts say software is under pressure from worries that AI will undercut subscription software while chip makers and memory names surge, with traders watching $240 as support.

items.name: Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bear 3X
items.about: Leveraged ETF that aims for three times the opposite of the daily move in a semiconductor index.
items.why: The fund fell 11.4% to $42.50 as semiconductor stocks rallied; it is built to move opposite chips by three times, so it falls when chips rise. It slipped further after hours as memory names jumped on SK Hynix's reported results.

items.name: XP Inc
items.about: Brazilian investment platform and broker offering brokerage, advisory and banking services.
items.why: Shares rose 1.6% to $15.96 on volume far above recent days. Posts cite Brazil political worries and say a promotional post claimed the stock fell sharply over the past week; they also mention a $180M buyback and a dividend. I could not confirm a specific catalyst.
